headline: Copper Prices Fall to Four-Month Low as Tech Weakness Saps Risk Appetite
summary: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell to $13,211.50 per metric ton, hitting its lowest level since July as technology stock sell-offs and dollar strength hurt commodity demand.
why: Copper is a key industrial metal widely considered a leading barometer for broad economic health and clean energy manufacturing.

impacts.name: Copper
impacts.why: Industrial metal demand expectations weakened due to technology sector weakness and currency strength.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Broader tech sector declines reduced investor risk appetite, while a firmer US dollar made dollar-priced metals more expensive.
